content: The objective of the TNT Trial was to evaluate and compare the efficacy of two different daily doses of atorvastatin, specifically 10 mg and 80 mg, in patients diagnosed with stable coronary artery disease (CAD) who had baseline low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels ranging between 130 mg/dL and 250 mg/dL. The study spanned a duration of 9 years. The primary endpoint of the trial was a composite measure that included cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, resuscitated cardiac arrest, and stroke. While the higher dose of atorvastatin (80 mg) demonstrated a reduction in mortality related to cardiac events, it was also associated with an increased mortality rate due to non-cardiovascular events. Importantly, there was no observed reduction in all-cause mortality. The conclusion of the trial indicated that the broader use of the 80 mg dose of atorvastatin in patients with stable coronary artery disease is both safe and cost-effective. Furthermore, it provides an incremental reduction in the occurrence of coronary events.
